# Documentation prompt for Microsoft.Graph/deviceEnrollmentConfigurations

<!-- Generated by azure-resource-downloader. Paste this prompt together with a resource YAML from this directory into an LLM. -->

You are a senior Microsoft cloud and endpoint-management consultant. Generate clear, accurate end-user documentation for the attached resource configuration.

Azure resource type: Microsoft.Graph/deviceEnrollmentConfigurations

About this resource type: An Intune device enrollment configuration, such as the Enrollment Status Page or enrollment restrictions.

Subtype guidance: Polymorphic (@odata.type): deviceEnrollmentLimitConfiguration, deviceEnrollmentPlatformRestrictionsConfiguration (default, all platforms), deviceEnrollmentPlatformRestrictionConfiguration (one platform), deviceEnrollmentWindowsHelloForBusinessConfiguration, windows10EnrollmentCompletionPageConfiguration (Enrollment Status Page), deviceEnrollmentNotificationConfiguration, deviceComanagementAuthorityConfiguration and windowsRestoreDeviceEnrollmentConfiguration (tenant-wide, not targetable); deviceEnrollmentConfigurationType values starting with 'default' mark the built-in defaults.

Permissions required to read this resource type:
- DeviceManagementServiceConfig.Read.All

Lifecycle notes for this resource type:
- Edits apply to new enrollments only; devices already enrolled are not affected.
- Restrictions: priority 1 is highest and only the highest-priority assigned policy applies; the default applies to everyone not covered and always to enrollments that aren't user-driven.
- Enrollment restrictions are a best-effort barrier for non-malicious users, not a security feature: compromised devices can misrepresent their attributes.
- Device limits (1 to 15 per user) can't apply to Windows co-managed, Group Policy, Entra join (including bulk), Autopilot or device enrollment manager enrollments; use the Entra ID device limit for those. Android and iOS/iPadOS OS version limits apply only to Company Portal enrollments.
- Platform restrictions: blocking personally owned Windows devices still admits Windows Autopilot, Group Policy or co-management, bulk provisioning package and device enrollment manager enrollments; Entra join in Windows setup or from Settings is blocked unless the device is Autopilot-registered or matches a Windows corporate identifier, and Autopilot for existing devices and Autopilot device preparation need a matching corporate identifier.
- Restrictions and the Windows Hello for Business enrollment policy are created, edited and reprioritised with the Intune Administrator Entra role (other built-in Intune roles are read-only); enrollment notifications also need Intune Administrator.
- Enrollment Status Page: a device-targeted profile wins over a user-targeted one, then the default; pre-provisioning and self-deploying apply device-targeted profiles only, and Group Policy enrollments and Autopilot device preparation don't use the ESP.
- Failed enrollments appear in Devices > Monitor > Enrollment failures with the reason and enrollment method; for iOS/iPadOS, macOS and Windows devices, the device's Enrollment page (under Monitor) lists the platform restriction and ESP profiles applied at first enrollment, with priority, target and filter.
- Platform restrictions: Android device administrator management is deprecated and no longer available on devices with Google Mobile Services.
